title: Opinions on my 3D workflow
author: Belmeez
selftext:
Hey all,

Like many of you, I am not in the gaming industry by any means but I love playing games and have stated making my own 3D ARPG using tools like Claude, meshy ai, and other ai tools for voice and music etc.

My current 3D asset workflow is:

1. Chat gpt generates concept art for the model.

2. That image is used in meshy to generate the low poly 3D asset and texture it.

3. I often remesh it so I can reduce the size without it losing a lot of its structure.

4. Get it into miximo and get the rig for it.

5. Download just the rig from miximo and 3D asset from meshy. (Miximo melts it for some reason)

6. Combine the rig and meshy model in blender.

7. Get more animations from miximo that fit the model.

8. Export as glb and use in godot.

This has worked the best for me so far but I still struggle a bit with variety of animations etc because I am limited to miximo.

What do you guys think of this workflow?

comments.author: fisj
comments.body:
You can also rig models with something like accuRig2, or even blender has some decent auto rigging tools and assistants. I'm not familiar with godot's pipeline for animations, but I find it hard to believe there wouldn't be a way to retarget animations from the unity asset store to the skeletons you make for your meshy models.

Look into retarget unity animations to godot or something like that.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: Nice, I will look into that! Thank you. Any thought about my other workflow pieces?

comments.author: whats_don_is_don
comments.body: Wait - why not just use Meshy's auto-rigging tool? I've been using that and it's been good.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: Not had a great experience with their rigging tool every time I have used it it has been wonky, especially the hand movements, as well as just basic walking and synchronization

comments.author: Final_Fantasy_VII
comments.body: That’s a nice workflow, regarding animation there are many Text to Animation programs out there like Deep motion,  you should try and most of them are free or provide free credits.

comments.author: superkickstart
comments.body: Hard to tell without seeing samples. It might produce good models, or it might produce really shit ones.

comments.author: Agreeable-Clerk-4819
comments.body: That workflow looks great. I’ve been testing the Hitem3D plugin to keep everything inside Blender for the initial generation . It saves a bit of friction not having to export and import from a browser. It’s been efficient for getting the base assets ready for manual refinement.
